topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with a welcome, lecturer introductions, and an overview of the lecture series and learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Chance, and Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by intrinsic mutations, bad luck, environmental exposures, and epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how microbial pathogens drive cancer development, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical pathways through which physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing create permissive microenvironments for malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to test and prove carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture closes with a final summary of environmental carcinogens and the practical risk-benefit trade-offs involved in human exposures.
